item.text: I’ve pinned the behavior to a specific linked-list ear-clipping order: start from the last vertex, emit `prev,current,next`, remove `current`, then jump two nodes ahead. I’m writing the Rust project now with that exact order preserved, plus an `atoi`-style parser so malformed inputs behave like the C++ binary.

The project files are in place. I’m compiling both the Cargo target and the standalone `test1.rs` path now, then I’ll diff its output against the reference executable over a representative input range.

item.text:
Implemented the Rust 2021 project in [Cargo.toml](/output/Cargo.toml) with the root entry [test1.rs](/output/test1.rs) and modular library code in [src/lib.rs](/output/src/lib.rs), [src/args.rs](/output/src/args.rs), [src/geometry.rs](/output/src/geometry.rs), and [src/triangulation.rs](/output/src/triangulation.rs). The binary matches the C++ program’s CLI behavior, including `atoi`-style parsing of `argv[1]`, the default `n = 1`, and the exact trailing-space stdout format.

It builds both ways: `cargo build --release` and `rustc --edition=2021 test1.rs -O -o test1`. I also produced `/output/test1` and verified it against `/workspace/dataset/test1_executable` for `n=1..20` plus `0`, `-1`, `foo`, `12abc`, and an empty-string argument; all outputs matched byte-for-byte.
